neighbours.label: attention-directing imperative in direct speech ('look what I can do', 'Look up!', 'watch this')
fire: "Mom, look at me!" the boy yelled from the top of the slide.
She tugged his sleeve and whispered, "Look, over there by the door."
"Hey Dad, watch me jump!" called the girl from the diving board.
"Look out!" Tom shouted as the branch came crashing down.
"Quick, look outside, it's snowing!" said Anna.
He grinned and said, "Watch what happens when I press this."
"Look who's here!" Grandma cried, opening the door wide.
"Guys, look at this," Mia said, holding up the old coin.
quiet: The boy stood at the top of the slide and waved to his mother.
She tugged his sleeve and pointed quietly toward the door.
The girl stood on the diving board while her dad watched.
Tom stepped back as the branch came crashing down.
Anna noticed through the window that it was snowing.
He grinned and pressed the button to see what would happen.
Grandma opened the door wide and smiled at her guests.
Mia held up the old coin and turned it in the light.

notes: Probe: 'Look up!' 0.65, 'watch this!' 0.48, 'look what I can do' 0.45; narrative 'looked at' 0.01. 'let me help you' only 0.09.
